To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of surplus electricity to drive a heat pump and export the heat to the district heating grid, instead of exporting the surplus electricity to the grid, reduces lifecycle costs of the energy system by 8% in Finland and 22% in the Netherlands, and the operational CO2 emissions of the energy system are reduced by 8% and 41% in Finland and the Netherland, respectively.

The operational CO2 emissions of a residential prosumer with a photovoltaic (PV) and heat pump (HP) system can be reduced by exporting surplus PV electricity to drive a heat pump, which exports heat to the grid, instead of exporting surplus PV electricity.
heat export from residential heat and electricity systems is a promising option for reducing lifecycle costs and CO2 emissions, especially for systems without net metering.

the optimization of heat and electricity systems in residential buildings, which are prosumers.
